why:
The denominator `v4 coverage` used to report against was the predecessor's obligation catalogue: 557 ids, and this repo's own reconciliation showed two thirds of them are PO-DL-nnn generated per phase and will never recur. Answering a coverage question against a denominator that is mostly one-off by construction is the same as not answering it.

These 17 are risk classes, not stack mechanics -- drawn from Google SRE PRR, AWS Well-Architected, 12-Factor and OWASP, plus the shapes that recurred across the predecessor's overlay corpus. They change on a multi-year cadence. Nine are marked `judgment`: only this project's own architecture answers them, and a web-only generator systematically misses them -- which is exactly the half a checker cannot reach either.

`answered_by` is hand-written. Whether two questions have anything in common is a judgement and no string comparison recovers it.

Mapping reviewed 2026-09-06 against current claim kinds. answered_by identifies a related mechanism, not proof that the whole category is covered. These mechanisms inspect bounded patterns; current covered categories are marked partial.

rows.trigger: Per data type, does the arch doc say which store is authoritative truth vs derived/projection/cache?
Does any handler get retried, delivered ≥once, or run concurrently with itself (webhooks, queues, retried calls, scheduled jobs across replicas)?
Does any operation write >1 record/store or do a multi-step mutation where partial failure or interleaving corrupts data (money/inventory/counters, write-then-publish, sagas)?
Does the system call any dependency that can fail transiently (network, DB, queue, cache, third-party API)?
Which external calls are irreversible, and who authorizes them?
Is every read AND write filtered by a server-trusted scope, never a client-supplied one?
Are there discrete, independently-verified guard tiers rather than one `isAuthenticated` check?
Does the system use any credential, and does any code/config cross a server→client bundle/serialization boundary?

rows.category: Centralized typed config, fail-fast at startup
rows.trigger: Does the project read env/config that, if missing/malformed, should crash at startup rather than deep in a request?

rows.category: Adapter boundary — no raw external types in domain
rows.trigger: Does the project call external SDKs/HTTP/ORM/broker libs whose native types could leak into domain logic?
Is there a stable run/correlation identity propagating across retries and into all logs/artifacts/stores?
Are there distinct runtime roles with each trigger source mapped, not one generic worker?

rows.category: Observability / drift / liveness of decoupled flows
rows.trigger: Does the system have background/decoupled flows or failure modes whose health an operator must observe, including ones that silently fall behind?

rows.category: Artifact / workspace / runtime-state lifecycle + destructive-op safety
rows.trigger: Is each directory/store given a role (workspace / runtime-temp / output) with lifecycle metadata, AND does any autonomous/scheduled operation delete / evict / truncate based on age/size/count (cleanup, GC, TTL, log-rotate, cache-evict, row-purge)?
Are there runtime-read descriptors (tool descriptions, prompt claims, schemas, pinned versions) where divergence from behavior is a correctness failure?
Does the platform mandate endpoints/webhooks/scopes/version pins that are architecture surfaces, not config trivia?
Does the system write secret/config files to disk, run scheduled/daemon processes, or own local artifacts on a host?
